6086.t: From συγγιγνώσκω (sŭngĭgnṓskō, “to agree with; to acknowledge; to excuse; to pardon”) + -μη (-mē); by surface analysis, συν- (sŭn-) + γνώμη (gnṓmē).

6026.t: Of foreign origin, perhaps connected to πάρδαλις (párdalis).

6032.t: Traditionally explained (such as by Frisk) as a derivative from πέρδομαι (pérdomai, “to fart”), due to the droning sound when partridges take wing.

6030.t: Uncertain. Some suggest the source is Proto-Indo-European *pleh₂- (“flat, broad, plain”), whereas others such as Beekes suggest a non-Indo-European origin.

6057.t: The suffix "-αρνο-" suggests a Pre-Greek origin.

6021.t: From Proto-Indo-European *(ts)ptyew- (“to spit, vomit”). Akin to Latin spuō, Albanian pështyj, Old English spīwan (English spew), Old Armenian թուք (tʻukʻ), Old Church Slavonic пльвати (plĭvati), Sanskrit ष्ठीवति (ṣṭhīvati).

6059.t: From Proto-Indo-European *tworHos (“seizer, encloser”), from Proto-Indo-European *twerH- (“to enclose”). Cognate to Proto-Slavic *tvȏrъ (“creature”) and Proto-Slavic *tvoriti (“to make”).

6022.t: From Proto-Indo-European *pewǵ- (“to punch”). Cognates include Latin pugnus, Lithuanian puši̇̀s, and Old English fyst (English fist).

6092.t: From σῦκον (sûkon, “fig”) + φαίνω (phaínō, “show”) + -της (-tēs, masculine agent-noun suffix).

6093.t: Verbal noun from συλλογίζομαι (sullogízomai, “to compute, infer”) + -μός (-mós).

6054.t: From either σκεῦος (skeûos, “vessel”) or σκευή (skeuḗ, “equipment”) + -άζω (-ắzō), both ultimately of the same origin.

6064.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *sper- Proto-Indo-European *-yeti Proto-Indo-European *spéryeti Proto-Hellenic *spéřřō Ancient Greek σπείρω (speírō) Proto-Hellenic *-ā́ Ancient Greek -α (-ā) ? Proto-Indo-European *sper- Proto-Indo-European *-h₂…

6083.t: Late Hellenistic Koine back-formation from ἕστηκα (héstēkă, “I have stood”), perfect of ἵστημι (hĭ́stēmĭ).

6058.t: According to Beekes, the phonetic variants listed above in the "Alternative forms" section prove Pre-Greek origin for this word.

6078.t: Maybe from Proto-Indo-European *strebʰ- (“to twist”), which στρέφω (stréphō, “to twist”) is also often derived from.

6039.t: The etymology is uncertain. Maybe related to σήθω (sḗthō, “to sift, bolt”) or perhaps a contamination of σαπρός (saprós, “rotten”) with an unknown word.

6082.t: From στυγέω (stugéō) + -νός (-nós), of uncertain origin, possibly from Proto-Indo-European *(s)tewg- (“to hit, push”) (compare Sanskrit तुज् (tuj, “to push, drive”)).

6043.t: Clearly related to σέλμα (sélmă, “deck of a ship”). These words have been compared to Old English selma and syll, and to German Schwelle (“threshold”), but phonetically this etymology is unconvincing.

6068.t: From the root of στείβω (steíbō, “to tread on, stamp on”).

6048.t: Possibly a loanword from Egyptian šnḏwt (“kilt”). Compare also Hebrew סָדִין (sadin, “bedsheet”).

6066.t: From *σπάργω (*spárgō, “to swaddle”), which is from the zero-grade of Proto-Indo-European *sper- (“to twist”) with a g-extension (perhaps via contamination with a verb of similar meaning, like εἴργω (eírgō, “to enclose”)).

6071.t: From στείβω (steíbō, “to tread, stamp”) + -η (-ē). The "cushion" and "padding" senses are from the custom of filling pillows and mattresses using shrub leaves.

6065.t: From σπάω (spắō, “to draw (a weapon)”) + -ων (-ōn, nominal suffix).

6096.t: Etymology tree Ancient Greek συν- (sŭn-) Ancient Greek πάσχω (páskhō)der.

6080.t: From Proto-Hellenic *stugéō, from Proto-Indo-European *stug-éyeti, from *(s)tewg- (“to push, hit”).
